steps.name: QC and sample alignment
steps.question: Do the 12 samples in log_expr.csv and metadata.csv align, and do treated vs control samples form coherent, outlier-free groups on a PCA/MDS of the log2(TPM+1) values?
steps.description: Load log_expr.csv (12,000 rows; first column holds gene identifiers, verify and use as row names) and metadata.csv (12 samples x 2 columns). Confirm which of the 13 expression columns are actual samples and drop any identifier/index column. Match expression columns to metadata sample IDs, confirm the condition column encodes exactly 'treated' and 'control' (6 each), and reorder columns to metadata row order. QC: PCA/MDS of the 12 samples colored by condition, inter-sample Pearson correlation heatmap, per-gene mean/variance summary, detection of low-expression genes (e.g., log2(TPM+1) < 1 in all samples) for optional filtering, and an outlier check. Report any sample-label mismatch or outlier sample explicitly; do not drop samples without flagging.
acceptance_criteria: PCA or MDS plot colored by condition produced; sample correlation heatmap produced
Any sample failing correlation/outlier criteria reported explicitly rather than silently removed
Output: a clean expression matrix (genes x 12 samples) plus sample QC plots written to the step's output directory

steps.name: Differential expression: treated vs control
steps.question: Which genes differ between the 6 treated and 6 control muscle samples, and by how much (log2 fold change, moderated t-test, BH-adjusted FDR)?
steps.description: Fit a limma linear model on the log2(TPM+1) matrix with design ~ condition (control as reference), apply empirical-Bayes moderation (eBayes) and treat-vs-control contrast. With n=6 per group and unpaired design there are no covariates to include; single batch so no batch term. Report logFC, moderated t, raw p, BH-adjusted FDR for all 12,000 genes; use robust eBayes and, if the mean-variance trend warrants it, trend=TRUE (voom is not applicable — no counts). Report counts of significant genes at FDR<0.05 and |logFC| thresholds (1.0 and 0.58 = 1.5x), and note that at 6 vs 6 only large effects are detectable.
acceptance_criteria: Full DE results table written (all 12,000 genes) with logFC, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, CI bounds
Counts of significant genes at FDR < 0.05 (up/down) reported
Gene identifiers in output remain exactly as delivered in log_expr.csv (no silent remapping)

steps.name: Result visualization
steps.question: How do the treated-vs-control differences distribute across magnitude, significance, and expression level, and do the top DE genes separate the two groups?
steps.description: From the T1S2 results table produce: a volcano plot (logFC vs -log10 FDR, labeling top genes by ggrepel), an MA-style plot (mean log2 expression vs logFC), and a heatmap of the top 30-50 DE genes (by FDR) across the 12 samples annotated by condition (pheatmap/ComplexHeatmap). Also write a ranked gene list ( moderated t statistic, signed) sorted for use as input to competitive gene-set testing in T1S4.
acceptance_criteria: Volcano plot with significant genes highlighted; top-N heatmap with condition annotation; ranked-statistics file for downstream gene-set testing
Plots written to output directory; ranked list restricted to genes present in the expression matrix

steps.name: Pathway-level summary
steps.question: Which biological pathways are shifted between treated and control samples, giving the gene-level differences a biological reading?
steps.description: Run competitive pathway testing on the moderated-t-ranked gene list against the WikiPathways human pathway gene sets (HGNC gene symbols; the staged GMT under /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/, splitting the '%'-delimited first field for readable set names). Use limma::camera (or fgsea) with the full matrix and condition design for inter-gene-correlation-aware testing, plus GSEA-style preranked testing as a cross-check. Report per-pathway direction (enriched in treated vs control), size, and FDR; restrict to pathways with >= 10 and <= 500 genes present in the matrix. If gene-symbol overlap between the matrix and the GMT is poor (< 50% of pathways with >= 10 genes), report the overlap honestly and interpret results as indicative only.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment results table: pathway, size, direction (enriched in treated vs control), FDR
Only pathways with >= 10 and <= 500 genes overlapping the expression matrix retained
If the GMT contains near-zero overlap with the 12,000 genes, report the overlap count explicitly and mark enrichment inconclusive rather than proceeding

plan.title: Treated vs control DE in log2(TPM+1) muscle RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 12,000-gene x 13-column log2(TPM+1) matrix with a 12-sample metadata table (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch). Because the facility delivered normalized log-scale values and no raw counts, count-based models (DESeq2/edgeR) are inappropriate; limma's linear-model framework on the log2 values is the standard, statistically correct approach for this data type. The plan: (1) align expression columns to metadata rows, verify the two extra expression columns are non-sample (e.g., an index column), and run sample-level QC (PCA, sample correlations, outlier check); (2) fit limma moderated t-tests for treated vs control across all 12,000 genes, with BH FDR and effect sizes; (3) visualize results (volcano, MA, top-gene heatmap); (4) test whether differential-expression signals converge on biological pathways using the WikiPathways human GMT via competitive gene-set testing (camera/fgsea), reporting the treatment-affected biology rather than only a gene list. With 6 vs 6 the study is powered only for large effects, so the plan reports effect sizes and confidence intervals alongside p-values and flags modest FDR-level results as supportive, not definitive.
